_about: Numbers cited by the robot-workload-benchmarking kit. Every value is one of three classes, given in its 'source' field: 'public' (a cited public paper/doc with URL), 'sibling' (a value already in ../nvidia-gpu-anatomy or ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics, cited by that kit's constants key or note), or 'illustrative' (a round number invented to explain an idea, never a measurement). NO number here is copied from any internal campaign. Load this file; do not retype the numbers into prose.

wbc_control_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative control-loop rate used in A4; a learned locomotion policy at 50 Hz is a common choice

wbc_deadline_illustrative.source: illustrative: the period of a 50 Hz loop is 20 ms, used in A4/B3 as the deadline

motor_bus_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative range for a motor-control board bus in A4; 'hundreds of Hz' is typical

perception_output_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative perception publish rate in A2/A0; soft-real-time perception commonly targets ~10 Hz

camera_frame_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative camera frame rate in A1/A2; 30 fps is a common depth-camera rate

audio_packet_framing_illustrative.source: illustrative microphone-array packet framing in A5 to show frames-per-packet sets message rate; 48 frames at 16 kHz is 3 ms

audio_sample_rate_illustrative.source: illustrative microphone sample rate in A5; 16 kHz is standard for speech models

nvfp4_available_board.source: ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/glossary.md (NVFP4; Thor only) — referenced generically in A6/B1

silero_vad_params_public.source: Silero VAD, https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad (model is sub-2M parameters; order-of-magnitude only)

openwakeword_window_public.source: openWakeWord, https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord (80 ms at 16 kHz melspectrogram hop window; order-of-magnitude)

vla_action_horizon_illustrative.source: illustrative action-chunk horizon in A6; see sibling C1 note for a real example (H=10)

vla_latency_example_sibling.source: ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json pi05_latency_measured.thor_fp8 — cited in A6 only as the sibling kit's worked example, not a new measurement

vla_replan_rate_example_sibling.source: ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json pi05_latency_predicted.thor_16bit re-plan — cited in A6 as the sibling example

mps_sm_cap_example_sibling.source: ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json mps_cap_wbc_p99 — the MPS SM-cap range that returned the example control loop under deadline; cited in A6/B4

clock_offset_target_illustrative.source: illustrative cross-machine clock-offset bound in B2; set below the smallest latency being measured

warmup_illustrative.source: illustrative warm-up before a measurement window in C4

window_illustrative.source: illustrative measurement-window length in C4; actual length comes from a sample-count rule

foreign_cpu_gate_illustrative.source: illustrative census threshold in C4: a window is suspect if un-accounted processes use more than ~0.3 cores

interference_factor_definition.source: definition used in C6; the ratio itself is computed per run, no fixed value

nsys_perturbation_illustrative.source: illustrative order of the observer effect in B4: enabling a timeline trace can add milliseconds of latency to the traced service
